conventions.convention: The source parameter is s and the library parameter is t=s⁻¹. The semilinear Hopf dictionary fixes E and F and sends K_h to D_{−h}; coordinate weights, including the central coordinate, are retained.

Charges satisfy m₁≥⋯≥m_l. Columns increase strictly from bottom to top and are read top to bottom in decreasing order. A≤B means equal total weight and dominance of every original column-prefix weight of A over that of B. Standard tableaux additionally have weakly increasing rows.

Finite column heights are n_j=m_j+1−inf(I), requiring I bounded below. Semi-infinite columns instead use a common ground tail and finite coordinate differences. Classical category-O constructions require finite n and bounded-below I; quantum constructions use compatible finite double cuts.
L_A is the ordinary-bar-fixed positive-s chart; T_A is the ordinary-bar-fixed negative-s chart. M_B=Σ_A d_{A,B}(s)L_A, and P_A=Σ_B d_{A,B}(s)M_B. P is generally not ordinary-bar fixed.

Both labelled monomial Gram matrices are B_ψ⁻¹. The source sesquilinear form conjugates its first argument; the reverse-factor form C is bilinear. On the highest constituent B₈=s⁻ᵃC₀, so G_up(A)=sᵃD_A and G_low(A)=s⁻ᵃP_A, with rectification of the lower label.
The classical highest-weight tuple is λ_{A,j}=a_j+j−1, with ρ_j=(n+1−2j)/2. Thus λ_{A,j}+ρ_j=a_j+(n−1)/2. The Fock weight indexes an entry multiset and is not a classical gl_n highest weight.

The entry stabilizer K differs from the column Levi subgroup J. Sorting uses the right place action (aw)_i=a_{w(i)}; w_A is shortest right modulo K and d(A)=w_A⁻¹ is shortest left. The positive-source chart uses the sign Hecke module at v=s, whereas the actual tensor action initially uses v=s⁻¹.

The source upper tableau signature cancels −+ pairs, raises the leftmost surviving −, and lowers the rightmost surviving +. Its associated-string Chevalley coefficients are [ε_i] and [φ_i], with errors in strictly shorter strings.

Semi-regular duality uses the graded restricted dual and internal homogeneous Hom, not unrestricted completed Hom. Ψ is contravariant on standard flags; F=DΨ is covariant from opposite standard flags to target costandard flags.

A normalized indecomposable tilting at A contains Δ(A) once at the bottom, with a standard-filtered quotient using strictly smaller labels. For a proper original lower ideal, Ringel duality gives an opposite highest-weight Serre quotient by complementary labels.
AC is explicitly assumed for the genuine finite parabolic summand and inherited categorical suppliers; the zero object has empty standard and costandard flags.

load_bearing.statement: For finite natural tensors, U_{a,b}(s)=(-s)^{ℓ(w_b)−ℓ(w_a)}Σ_{z∈K}(-1)^{ℓ(z)}P_{w_az,w_b}(s⁻²), and D_{a,b}(s)=s^{ℓ(w_b)−ℓ(w_a)}P_{d_bw₀,d_aw₀}(s⁻²). The ordinary-bar exterior embedding sends wedge L_A to ambient L_{a(A)} and gives the stated signed wedge inverse coefficients in either factor order, independently of category O.

Assuming AC and bounded-below I, the positive-source transition is the entry-stabilizer antispherical/sign family, while the genuine mixed singular-ambient/parabolic-Levi composition matrix satisfies [M(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)=Σ_{C∼col B}(-1)^{ℓ(B,C)}P_{d(C)w₀,d(A)w₀}(1).

Assuming AC, the algebraic semi-regular bimodule gives the restricted free/cofree equivalence and an exact contravariant equivalence Ψ:F(bar Δ)→F(Δ)ᵒᵖ preserving tableau labels and matching central summands while reversing their order. F=DΨ is an exact covariant equivalence F(bar Δ)≃F(∇), with F(bar Δ(A))≅∇(A). No arbitrary-object or unrestricted-Hom equivalence is asserted.

Assuming inherited AC, every finite cut of the full ordered minuscule wedge tensor, in either order, has the balanced source upper triple with lifts L_A. The kernel of E_i^{n+1} is spanned by L_A with ε_i(A)≤n; the associated rank-one string equations are E_iL_A=[ε_i(A)]_sL_{ẽ_iA} and F_iL_A=[φ_i(A)]_sL_{f̃_iA}, modulo strictly shorter strings.

Assuming AC and the positive biadjoint residue sl₂ action, the completed coincident-eigenvalue affine-Hecke algebra and its partial central fibres give divided-functor head/socle control. Consequently e_iL(A) and f_iL(A) are zero or self-dual indecomposables with simple isomorphic head and socle labelled ẽ_iA and f̃_iA; vanishing is exactly absence of the crystal edge.

In a finite genuine integral parabolic central summand over C, assuming AC, standard-filtered objects are exactly those N with Ext¹(N,∇_λ)=0 for every λ, equivalently all positive Ext groups vanish; the dual costandard criterion also holds. Flag categories are closed under direct summands, and normalized indecomposable tiltings are unique when they exist.

Assuming inherited AC, finite Fock cuts carry an involutive, parenthesization-independent ordinary tensor bar satisfying ψM_A=M_A+Σ_{B<A}Z[s±¹]M_B. Upper-cut inclusions and common-bottom-tail embeddings commute with this bar and preserve the actual charts and bases.

Assuming inherited AC, the vacuum generates the multiplicity-one highest constituent with normalized projection π. S_A=πM_A and D_A=πL_A, for standard A, are its respective standard-monomial and source dual-canonical bases. πL_A vanishes exactly off the standard labels; the integral kernel is the saturated direct summand spanned by those off-standard L_A.

Assuming AC and the actual tableau parabolic data, F(bar M(A))=∇(A), F(bar P(A))=T(A), and (T(A):M(B))=[bar M(B):bar L(A)]. The full-block Ringel dual is the opposite-parabolic block; a proper original lower ideal has the corresponding opposite highest-weight Serre quotient.

Assuming AC and the genuine tableau K₀/Fock identification at s=1, for every label A, [L(A)]=L_A, [P(A)]=P_A and [T(A)]=T_A. These are ungraded specializations; tilting coefficients use the opposite/reverse-column composition matrix.

concerns.concern: Two short justifications need to be explicit. First, the Statement identifies c_j with elementary functions of x₁,…,x_i while presenting relations h_{r−i+1}=⋯=h_r=0 at an arbitrary coincident eigenvalue. These relations require shifted coordinates x_j−a: for r=i=1 and eigenvalue a≠0, the raw operator x₁ equals a in the fibre, whereas the displayed relation is c₁=0. Specify that the polynomial coordinates have been shifted. [Chuang–Rouquier §3.2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0407205) makes this shift explicit. Second, step 1.2 only names 'the two-Koszul socle computation'. The reconstruction is short: compute top Tor over R=C[c₁,…,c_i] using the Koszul resolutions on the defining regular sequence and on the variables; this gives a one-dimensional socle in degree Σ deg(h_j)−Σ deg(c_j)=i(r−i). The cited coinvariant lemma alone does not establish this for Z_{i,r}.

F4 attributes 'longest permutations reverse Bruhat order' to lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations, but that item's Statement (a)–(e) does not state longest-element reversal. The assertion is correct and follows immediately from its rank criterion: reversing values replaces R_x(m,h) by m−R_x(m,N−h), and reversing positions gives the analogous complementary-prefix formula. Include this elementary derivation or cite an exact supplier.

The displayed D and N use standards as rows and simples as columns, as required by the later projective rows Dᵗ and tilting rows Nᵗ. Earlier batch notation instead defines D_{A,B}=d_{A,B}(1) with simple rows and standard columns. Explicitly state the example's transposed convention at its first matrices and in F2. The numerical matrices and finite-ideal quotient agree under the row-by-standard convention. Also qualify step 1.1's 'all ordinary S₃ Kazhdan-Lusztig values at 1 being 1' by 'for comparable indices'; the off-interval values are zero.
